pack.name: A Bestiary of the Harrowmoor
pack.author: Devon
pack.description: Ten monsters for levels 1 to 6, written for the wet lead country around Cold Harrow and usable anywhere. Every one of them carries the two fields Phase 3 added — reach in cells, and the reactions the engine actually implements — and every one has the lore line a critical Recall Knowledge prints, written as the thing a player could act on. No adventure, no scenes: this is stock for somebody else's encounters.

monsters.name: Moor Shrike
monsters.lore: It spits the barb and then will not close for two rounds — walk at it and it has nothing left.
monsters.desc: A bird the size of a terrier that has learned to keep a larder. The larder is a blackthorn, and it is not always birds on it.

monsters.name: Lantern-Wisp
monsters.lore: It cannot cross running water and it always tries to, which is how you drown one.
monsters.desc: A light at knee height that keeps a polite twenty feet ahead of you and has never once led anybody to a road.

monsters.name: Tollhouse Swarm
monsters.lore: It is one animal for the purposes of being hit and several hundred for the purposes of being frightening — fire moves it, blades barely do.
monsters.desc: Every rat that ever lived under the toll-house on the Thrapp road, moving as one opinion.

monsters.name: Cairn-Hound
monsters.lore: It guards a stone, not a place. Get the stone between you and it and it will not come round.
monsters.desc: Somebody was buried well enough to be given a dog. The dog took the job more seriously than the burial did.

monsters.name: Ash-Vicar
monsters.lore: The sermon needs two people in earshot. Spread out and it has to walk instead, and it is very bad at walking.

powers.name: The Short Sermon
powers.flavor: It gets through about four lines of a funeral and the fourth line is the one that lands.

monsters.desc: Buried in its vestments under a chapel that burned in the same year as everything else around here.

monsters.name: Fen-Troll
monsters.lore: It closes wounds in standing water and cannot in fire. Fight it on dry stone or bring a torch and be quick.
monsters.desc: Nine feet of patient grey nothing standing in water up to its knees, waiting for the same thing it was waiting for last year.

monsters.name: Hollow Knight
monsters.lore: The shield is the whole creature. Break the arm that holds it — anything that disarms it ends the fight early.
monsters.desc: Armour standing at attention with a hundred and twenty years of moor water in the joints and nothing at all inside.

monsters.name: Quarry-Golem
monsters.lore: It only steps where the ground was quarried. Off the cut stone it is slow, and it knows it.
monsters.desc: Somebody in the lead country worked out how to make the stone do the lifting, and then worked out nothing else at all.

monsters.name: Drowned Choir
monsters.lore: It sings to whoever is nearest and cannot sing to two people at once — the one it is looking at is the one it is spending on.

powers.name: The Water Part
powers.flavor: They take a breath together, which they should not be able to do, and everyone near them takes one too.

monsters.desc: Eleven voices that went into the water on the same afternoon and have been holding the same chord since.

monsters.name: Mire-Wyrm
monsters.lore: It cannot turn in under thirty feet. A fight in a passage is a fight it loses; a fight on open moor is not.

powers.name: Sour Breath
powers.flavor: It opens something that is not quite a mouth and the peat between you goes the colour of tea.

monsters.desc: The reason the lead country has drainage engines and no ploughs. It was here before the mine and it will be here after the argument about the mine.
